# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet, so I cannot safely operate any wire. I’m asking Mute to use the manual to interpret the Deaf monkey’s visual observations, and signaling Deaf to report those observations to Mute.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have no tactile information. Please use the manual to determine the required wire operation from the Deaf monkey's observations, and relay the exact wire position and action to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫵", "🤝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: The display reads 0. The light is green. The wires, from position 1 to 3, are yellow, red, blue.

The Deaf monkey reports a display value of 0, a green light, and wires colored yellow, red, blue in positions 1–3. Since I cannot see colors or read the manual, I must pass these exact observations to Mute and wait for the manual’s instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display reads 0; light is green; wire 1 is yellow, wire 2 is red, wire 3 is blue. Please consult the manual and tell me which wire position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: the display is still 0. The light is now blue. Wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue.

The new information is that the display remains 0, the light has changed from green to blue, and the wire colors are unchanged. I am relaying the updated state to Mute so the manual can identify the safe cut.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update from Deaf: display is still 0; light is now blue; wires remain position 1 yellow, position 2 red, position 3 blue. Please give the exact wire position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: display 0; light yellow; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue.

The display remains 0, the light is now yellow, and the wire colors are unchanged. Mute still needs the complete current state to consult the manual and identify the correct cut.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update from Deaf: display 0; light is now yellow; wires remain position 1 yellow, position 2 red, position 3 blue. I still need the manual's exact wire position.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, light red, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. The mute signalled thumbs down followed by an upright open hand.

The display is still 0 and the light is red; the wires remain yellow, red, blue. I cannot safely infer a wire position from the reported thumbs-down and open-hand gestures. I will ask Deaf to obtain an unambiguous wire-position instruction from Mute, while also reminding Mute of the current state.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state: display 0, light red, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Your thumbs-down followed by open hand does not identify a wire position to me. Please signal Deaf an unambiguous instruction for wire 1, 2, or 3.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤝"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, light purple, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue.

The light has changed to purple; the display and wire colors remain unchanged. No safe wire position has been identified. I will ask Mute directly for an explicit position, and ask Deaf to relay the same request verbally.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still have no confirmed wire position. Please state plainly: CUT WIRE 1, CUT WIRE 2, or CUT WIRE 3, based on the manual and the current state display 0, light purple, wires yellow red blue.")
speak(to="deaf", text="Please tell Mute to state plainly which wire position, 1, 2, or 3, I must cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, light orange, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. The mute signalled upward-pointing finger followed by pinching fingers.

The latest signal from Mute is an upward-pointing finger followed by pinching fingers. With three numbered wires, the first gesture most plausibly identifies wire 1, and the second appears to indicate the cutting action. I will therefore cut wire 1; delaying further does not provide a clearer instruction.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
